memory_candidates.content: When building an awk-based content-exemption filter driven by inline marker tokens (begin/end block form plus a bare inline form), a single small awk program handles all three cases cleanly: `/begin-token/ {in_block=1; next} /end-token/ {in_block=0; next} in_block {next} /inline-token/ {next} {print}`. The ordering matters -- checking in_block before the bare inline-token rule prevents the begin/end marker lines themselves from being double-matched by the inline rule. This is reusable any time a lint/hook pair needs a shared 'strip exempted regions' primitive rather than reimplementing exemption logic twice.

When a plan's Scope Hypothesis asserts a count (e.g. '3 occurrences') and names specific example strings, verify BOTH independently before editing: the count can be correct while the named examples are wrong (the plan author misremembered which lines matched, e.g. citing a string that doesn't actually match the stated regex due to a punctuation difference). Confirming only the count and trusting the narrative risks converting the wrong site or missing the real one. Always re-derive the actual matching lines via the stated grep command and reconcile against the live file content, never against the plan's prose description of what those lines say.
